summary.text: 雨 is a picture of rain falling from above. Early forms varied, and oracle-bone inscriptions use it for both “rainwater” and “to rain.”

formation.text: Pictographic: the graph depicts rain falling downward. Early versions do not show one fixed arrangement; the claim that the top stroke was simply added later is not confirmed by the variable forms described here.

components.text: The whole graph is pictorial. Many oracle-bone forms have a stroke above two or three drops; the drops sometimes touch it, and an extra stroke may be decorative. A later account divides the graph into heaven, cloud, and rainwater, but this does not establish those as fixed parts of the early forms.

history.text: The early designs vary. In Western Zhou forms, the outer rain shape is connected into a line; in some Warring States forms, the drops look water-like. The curated seal-style image is a modern reconstruction, not an ancient inscription.

One account says the top horizontal stroke was added later. Other descriptions report early variation, including connecting and decorative strokes, so the timing of that stroke is unresolved. No cited account establishes graphic corruption.

uncertainties.text: The cited inscription records support early uses, but their individual dates are not given. They do not establish the first attested date, a single fixed early design, or a precise sequence for the upper stroke.
An ancient explanation divides the graph into heaven, cloud, and rainwater. That account does not establish these as fixed components in the variable early forms.

senses.text: Cited oracle-bone inscriptions use 雨 as a noun for rainwater. This is an early attested use, not necessarily the graph’s original meaning.
Other cited oracle-bone inscriptions use 雨 as a verb meaning “to rain.” The noun and verb are attested in the same broad corpus; which use came first is not established.
Later literary examples use 雨 as a transitive verb. They attest this use but do not establish its chronology or development from the intransitive verb.
雨 has the current gloss “rainy”; its development and chronology are not established here.

limitations.text: The cited inscription numbers are not individually dated, and later literary examples do not establish a detailed chronology or semantic path among the noun and verb uses.

items.period: Small seal / Shuowen seal-script style; Commons labels it Shuowen seal style, without dating the particular digital drawing.
items.tradition: Chinese small seal script (modern digital vector reconstruction)
items.caption: A modern vector reconstruction of 雨 in a Shuowen seal-script style. This later rendering retains the enclosing form and marks representing falling rain; the source does not date this particular drawing.
items.alt: Black seal-script-style 雨, with a horizontal top stroke, a tall enclosing outline, a central vertical stroke, and four short marks inside.
items.selection_reason: Offers a legible comparison for the rain graph described in the historical accounts, while its modern reconstruction status is clear. It does not establish the appearance or date of an ancient inscription.
